tasks.title: figure_ocr_available() reports False although USE_OCR=1, tesseract.exe exists at the documented path, and 14,397 figure rows were produced
tasks.needs_main_reason: the diagnosis matters more than the measurement - a previous pass wrote a green-but-vacuous test around this exact ambiguity, and the record holds two mutually contradicting claims about the same environment
tasks.verify: Name which candidate cause holds, each falsifiable: (a) .env is not loaded in the pytest process, (b) TESSERACT_PATH is unset in .env (confirmed - only .env.example:78 mentions it, commented out) and the Tesseract directory is not on PATH, (c) figure_ocr_available() gates on something other than the binary. Then figure_ocr_available() returns True in the same interpreter environment `pytest test_figure_ocr.py -q` runs in, or every doc claiming OCR is available is corrected to match reality.
tasks.why_model: a root-cause hunt across config loading, PATH and feature detection where a plausible-but-wrong answer is cheap to produce and already was once
tasks.why_mode: needs the surrounding record - the contradiction sits between the run log, the docs and the live environment, not inside one file
tasks.why_lane: writes .env, the global runtime config every concurrently-running task inherits

tasks.title: Ingest DeepSID metadata through its JSON API rather than scraping the SPA's HTML
tasks.verify: A DeepSID JSON endpoint is fetched and turned into an ingestible card, covered by a test in test_sid_ingest.py against a recorded/stubbed response (no live network in the suite). `pytest test_sid_ingest.py -q` green, and kb/ingest/__init__.py's _EXPECTED_METHODS guard extended rather than weakened for any new mixin method.
tasks.why_model: an unspecified third-party API contract plus a new network failure surface - the shape must be understood before it can be coded, and guessing an endpoint is cheap
tasks.why_mode: the design call (which endpoints, one document per tune or per collection) reshapes the existing one-file-one-document ingest contract

tasks.title: requires-python is '>=3.10' but wikigen/data.py:326 puts a backslash inside an f-string expression, which needs 3.12
tasks.blocked_on: Which way to reconcile: bump requires-python to >=3.12 (dropping 3.10/3.11 installs), or hoist the regex out of the f-string so the declared 3.10 floor becomes true again. The second is a two-line change; the first is a support-policy decision only the user can make.
tasks.verify: Either pyproject.toml reads requires-python = ">=3.12" and README.md/CLAUDE.md's 'Python 3.10+' claims are updated to match, or wikigen/data.py:326 holds no backslash inside an f-string expression and the file parses under a 3.10 ast.parse.
tasks.why_model: once the policy is chosen the edit is one line plus doc follow-through
tasks.why_mode: an install-floor decision - either answer is defensible and the user owns which Pythons this supports

tasks.title: Decide whether to take a third-party LHA dependency so HVSC's .lha archives can be ingested
tasks.blocked_on: Python has no stdlib LHA support. Ingesting HVSC in its native distribution format means adding a third-party decompressor as a runtime dependency; the user owns whether this project takes one, or whether users are expected to unpack to .zip first.
tasks.verify: Either .lha files ingest end-to-end with a covering test in test_sid_ingest.py, or TO-DOS.md records the decision not to support .lha and states what users should do instead.
tasks.why_model: once the dependency call is made the implementation mirrors the existing .zip branch
tasks.why_mode: adding a runtime dependency is the user's call, not a judgement to delegate
tasks.why_lane: writes pyproject.toml (shared with pyproject-requires-python-understates-312) and kb/ingest/_extraction.py (shared with deepsid-json-api-ingestion)
